title: Qatar Dynasty
capsule: The Al-Thani dynasty established its authority over the Qatar peninsula from the 1820s, when Mohammed bin Thani emerged as the principal tribal leader of the Doha settlement after British East India Company actions disrupted the earlier power structure. In 1868 British Political Resident Colonel Lewis Pelly concluded an agreement with Mohammed bin Thani that effectively recognized Qatar as a distinct polity separate from Bahrain, marking the formal beginning of Al-Thani suzerainty. An Ottoman protectorate was imposed between 1871 and 1916, when the Anglo-Qatari Treaty transferred protective relations exclusively to Britain.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Qatar's political boundaries in the 19th century were poorly defined; the peninsula's outer coastline is clear but internal tribal divisions and the border with Saudi Arabia were not formally demarcated until the 20th century.
